newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to turn coal region into huge leisure spot.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to turn coal region into huge leisure spot.

text.p: South Korea on Tuesday unveiled an ambitious plan to build a large-scale leisure resort to inject new life into the country's once-thriving coal mining region.
The Ministry of Construction and Transportation said 2.54 trillion won ($2.93 billion) would be invested in a 436.9 million square metre site in mountainous and picturesque Kangwon province.
A ministry statement said abandoned coal towns would be transformed with the addition of ski trails, hotels, golf courses, condominiums and casinos by the year 2005.
"This is aimed at reviving the regional economy in areas devasted by a sharp drop in the demand for coal," said Ahn Choong-hwan, assistant director of the Construction and Transportation Ministry.
Coal mines in the country's eastern mountains provided the fuel that helped to propel South Korea into the leading ranks of the world's industrialised nations.
But only eight mines now operate in the area, down from 168 in 1988, due to a rapid shift to cleaner fuels such as liquified petroleum gas (LPG) and oil.
According to ministry figures, the area's population is around 260,000, compared to 440,000 in 1988.
The South Korean government, aware of the coal industry's dismal prospects, has run a rationalisation programme against expensive and inefficient mines since 1989.
"Building a leisure spot there is the best choice," said Ki Jung-sun, a researcher at the Coal Industry Promotion Board.
"Even though it is not attractive from a manufacturing point of view, the place is blessed with clean air, a nice landscape and a lot of snow," he said.
Of the total 2.54 trillion won required for the development project, some 439 billion won would be invested by the central government in infrastructure.
Some 1.93 trillion would be financed by the private sector and the rest by the provincial government.
The news caused share prices of mining companies, which own real estate in the area, to surge on Tuesday in Seoul trading. The mining sub-index soared 7.42 percent to 1,262.64.
Coal miner Dong Won Co Ltd rose the daily limit of eight percent, or 3,800 won, to 52,400 won, and Daesung Resources Co Ltd was up 7,700 won to 107,000.
Young Poong Mining and Construction Co Ltd, a gold miner, rose 3,200 won to 47,300.
"It's really good news. Those companies will earn a lot of money from soaring land prices in the area," said Hwang Chang-joong, analyst at LG Securities.
But brokers said the impact would be short-lived as the shares have already climbed 100 to 200 percent since the Kangwon provincial government submitted the plan for approval last August.
"Given the growing number of holiday makers, the future prospect of the business looks promising," Ahn said.
He forecast the resort area would attract about 1.2 million tourists a year.
(Conversion $1 = 867.80)
